assessment: The incumbent provides a predictable conversational routine and printed access; seven frequent attendees explicitly valued its repeated structure (H3-O6). Its benefit is nevertheless uneven: five occasional attendees struggled to enter a conversation familiar to their partner, a concrete limitation on assuming predictability makes participation easy for everyone. Familiarity causing that difficulty remains a hypothesis. Success is unestablished: useful practice was reported on 49/72 returned slips, correct preparation on 48/72, and coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Missing slips, untimed speaking and unlinked responses limit inference.

openings.claim: A brief mutual introduction to each prompt, followed by equal speaking turns, may make the existing routine easier to enter without prior attendance or public proficiency labels.
openings.delta: Preserve the familiar session sequence but print a self-contained entry prompt and turn instructions on existing sheets; reserve their time within the 75 minutes.
openings.prediction: If conversational entry and unequal turns limit practice, entry difficulty and within-pair speaking imbalance should decrease even when pair-formation time stays similar. Improvement only in pairing time would not support this account.
openings.probe: Alternate ordinary and entry-supported rounds, reversing order in another session. Observe anonymous speaking durations and partner changes; collect round-specific usefulness and entry-difficulty responses. Include planning and printing in weekly coordination totals.
assumptions: Participants accept turn instructions and can use the entry prompts.
Observation fits existing volunteer time; otherwise restrict the sampled pairs.
More balanced speaking need not be more useful and must be checked separately.

openings.claim: Confusion between current and earlier preparation tasks may contribute to incorrect task identification; a dated next-session box could reduce that confusion.
openings.delta: Add one clearly dated preparation instruction to each existing paper sheet, retaining optional messaging and allowing preparation-free participation.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers should fall when the dated box is present; unchanged errors despite correct on-sheet lookup would favor recall or instruction-comprehension problems over document ambiguity.
openings.probe: Compare ordinary and boxed sheets across sessions using anonymous unaided task identification followed by on-sheet lookup. Record blank and earlier-task answers separately, paper-only access, total weekly coordination time and conversational usefulness.
assumptions: The next task can be fixed before printing.
Adding the box requires little recurring volunteer effort.
Unaided identification and lookup are measured consistently.
